newsitem.title: GERMANY: German securities outflow slowed in May - Buba.
newsitem.headline: German securities outflow slowed in May - Buba.

text.p: The net outflow of securities investment in Germany fell in May to a net 6.1 billion marks compared with 11.6 billion in April, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday.

"The fall of net capital exports in the portfolio sector is attributable in the first place to stronger engagement from abroad with the domestic capital markets," the German central bank said in a monthly statement.
Foreign investors spent a net 5.1 billion marks on German securities in May having sold a net 500 million marks in April.
Buying interest from abroad focused on the equity market, the Bundesbank said, with net buys of 2.8 billion marks compared with net sales of 4.5 billion marks the month before.
Foreign investors continued to hold back from the German bond market however, purchasing only a net 700 million marks in fixed income securities in May compared with 4.3 billion marks in April.
And at the same time, German spending on foreign securities remained high at 11.2 billion marks, just up from 11.1 billion in April.
Demand from the German side focused particularly on foreign currency bonds, the Bundesbank said.
Long-term funds were also exported via direct investments, which totalled a net 1.4 billion marks, down from 2.5 billion in April.
